subsystem: Core brain, model routing, safety, budget, resident app
summary: The brain (agent/core.py) is big, heavily tested and works the same in every mode, and the always-on resident app you launch (tray, Ctrl+Space, dashboard, scheduler, awareness) is wired and has its own tests. But resident mode, which is the only mode you use, skips several start-up steps that only main.py does: sub-agents are never switched on, the nightly reflection and weekly self-review are never scheduled, the skill curator never runs, and the dashboard's Guardian/Time Capsule panels are never connected. Separately, the morning briefing cannot be scheduled at all (a confirmed crash in the trigger code), every 'risky' tool (run Python, run a skill, make an image, press Enter in a browser) is always refused in resident mode with no way to say yes, and DeepSeek errors skip the friendly error/fallback path and can hang for up to 10 minutes on a bad connection.

gaps.issue: Sub-agents never work in resident mode, the only mode you use. main.py switches the orchestrator on; app/resident.py never does, so spawn_subagent and run_plan always answer 'Orchestrator not initialised.'
gaps.fix_hint: Call orchestrator.set_agent_factory(AgentCore) in run_resident (better: move it into a shared boot helper next to schema.init_all) and add a wiring test that boots both paths.
gaps.how_confirmed: Grepped the whole repo for set_agent_factory / _agent_factory: the only production setter is main.py:285. Ran a snippet in a fresh process: orchestrator.spawn('researcher','t') -> 'Orchestrator not initialised.'

gaps.issue: The morning briefing can never be scheduled: briefing passes a timezone in trigger_params and the scheduler adds timezone='UTC' again, so CronTrigger raises 'multiple values for keyword argument timezone', _make_trigger returns None, and schedule() reports 'Unknown trigger_type: cron'. Enabling it on the dashboard silently fails. The default timezone is also America/New_York.
gaps.fix_hint: In _make_trigger, use params.pop('timezone', 'UTC'); default the briefing timezone to Asia/Beirut; add a test for install_briefing_task.
gaps.how_confirmed: Ran scheduler._make_trigger('cron', {'hour':8,'minute':0,'timezone':'Asia/Beirut'}) and it printed the TypeError and returned None. grep shows no test calls install_briefing_task.

gaps.issue: In resident mode every pattern-matched 'risky' tool is always refused, even when you yourself asked by hotkey or on the dashboard: run_python, python_exec, run_skill, generate_image, browser_press Enter, browser clicks on submit/send, sms_send, update_system_prompt, register_new_tool. The same goes for any bash/write_file/edit_file call the model reviewer flags, or every one of them when the reviewer can't be reached (offline or slow internet). There is no approve button anywhere.
gaps.evidence: app/resident.py:138-159 (resident_confirm returns False), 251-252; agent/safety.py:7-31, 103-115; agent/command_review.py:35-40; config.py:217
gaps.fix_hint: Route resident confirmations to a dashboard/Companion/phone approval with a timeout (reuse the approvals or pending_actions UI), and let an owner turn (by_owner=True) confirm by voice. Set SAFETY_REVIEW_MODEL to a local ollama model so it works offline.
gaps.how_confirmed: Read resident_confirm and safety.check; grepped for other set_confirm_fn callers (only node_worker.py:128, and only when unset, and resident overrides it afterwards). agent/approvals.py only covers memory/skill writes, not safety confirmations.

gaps.issue: DeepSeek (your model) errors bypass the error handling: core.run catches only anthropic.APIError, but the DeepSeek adapter raises openai.* errors. So no OpenRouter fallback and no friendly message; in resident mode you hear 'Something went wrong: Connection error'. The OpenAI client is also built with its defaults (600-second read timeout, 2 retries), not API_MAX_RETRIES, so on a bad Lebanese connection one turn can hang for many minutes while holding the turn lock.
gaps.evidence: agent/core.py:4138-4161; agent/provider.py:514-533 (OpenAIAdapter, no timeout/max_retries), 575-578; agent/resilience.py:40-67 (anthropic types only)
gaps.fix_hint: Translate openai.APIConnectionError/RateLimitError/APIStatusError into the resilience categories (or catch openai.APIError next to anthropic.APIError), and pass timeout=(e.g. 60s) and max_retries=config.API_MAX_RETRIES when building OpenAI(...).
gaps.how_confirmed: Ran a snippet: issubclass(openai.APIConnectionError, anthropic.APIError) is False; openai.OpenAI(...).timeout is read=600, max_retries=2. grep found no 'openai.' error handling in agent/ or tests/. resident _do_turn (app/resident.py:392-404) catches Exception and speaks the raw message.

gaps.issue: Resident mode skips other start-up steps that only main.py does: the 'Nightly reflection' and 'Weekly self-evaluation' scheduled tasks are never created, the morning briefing is never installed, the Skill Curator thread never runs, saved skills are not pre-loaded (list_skills is empty until one is run by name), the vault/Constellation are not initialised at boot, and the dashboard's Guardian and Time Capsule panels are never connected (always empty, and their toggle does not reach the running monitor).
gaps.fix_hint: Move all shared boot steps into one function (like schema.init_all) that both main.py and run_resident call; add a test asserting both paths call it.
gaps.how_confirmed: Grepped for set_guardian, set_timecapsule, skills.load_all, init_vault, constellation init, install_briefing_task, 'Nightly reflection', CURATOR_ENABLED: each appears only in main.py. Read server.py:1036-1062: the endpoints return an empty log when the ref is None.

gaps.issue: Cron schedules run in UTC, and nothing tells the model so. 'Every day at 8' fires at 10:00 or 11:00 Beirut time; the built-in nightly reflection (hour 3) and weekly review (Mon 8:00) are also UTC. Fixed-date reminders ('2026-12-01 09:00') are read as UTC too.
gaps.evidence: agent/scheduler.py:68-70, 184; agent/core.py:1365-1375 (tool description has no timezone); main.py:330, 345
gaps.fix_hint: Schedule in the PC's local timezone (tzlocal) or add an APEX_TIMEZONE setting, and say which zone in the schedule_task tool description.
gaps.how_confirmed: Read _make_trigger and the BackgroundScheduler(timezone='UTC') constructor, and the tool schema text at core.py:1365-1375; tests/test_scheduler.py only uses UTC.

gaps.issue: Budget reservations left by a crash or power cut are never released and never expire. They keep counting against today's (and every later day's) $5 cap, and there is no dashboard button to clear them. Repeated power cuts slowly eat the daily allowance until paid calls are refused.
gaps.evidence: agent/budget.py:157-162 (no time filter on budget_reservations), 241-249; agent/telemetry.py:150-153 (the only release, after a recorded response)
gaps.fix_hint: Expire reservations older than, say, an hour (counting them as estimated spend once), or add a 'clear stuck reservations' action on the budget panel.
gaps.how_confirmed: Ran a snippet against a temp DB: reserve() a deepseek-flash call (~$0.07), skipped record(), switched to session 2 -> reservations() still showed daily_reserved 0.0702.

gaps.issue: The $2 'session' cap covers the whole life of the resident process (one session id per boot). Background awareness/cortex calls count too, so a resident left running for days can hit the cap and refuse every paid call until restarted, with a message that does not say a restart clears it.
gaps.fix_hint: Raise the session default for resident mode, roll the session over daily, or make the message say 'restart Apex or raise session_usd on the dashboard'.
gaps.how_confirmed: Read the session_id lifecycle (telemetry.set_session once in run_resident) and the _limit_error session branch.

gaps.issue: The Control page offers about 34 settings that config.py hard-codes and never reads from .env (for example SMART_ROUTING_ENABLED, MAX_ITERATIONS, MAX_SUBAGENTS, THINKING_BUDGET, CURATOR_ENABLED, PROACTIVE_ENABLED). Saving one says 'takes effect when Apex restarts', but it never does, which is the exact trap set_setting's own docstring says it prevents.
gaps.fix_hint: Only list keys that config.py reads through getenv/_flag (or make those constants env-readable).
gaps.how_confirmed: Ran an AST snippet over config.py: 34 top-level UPPERCASE assignments with no getenv/_flag/environ, including the 7 named. Checked that config.py has no generic env-override loop (grep for globals()/setattr found none).

gaps.issue: Resident start-up messages say "Say 'Apex' or press Ctrl+Space" even though the wake word is off by default, and the hotkey text is hard-coded, not taken from RESIDENT_GLOBAL_HOTKEY.
gaps.fix_hint: Build the message from WAKE_WORD_ENABLED and the configured hotkey.

gaps.issue: Tray 'Open dashboard' opens the configured host/port, not the address the dashboard actually bound to (main.py and the Companion use the real one).

Autostart at login launches main.py --resident directly, not the platform launcher. A login start has no Celine voice server, no restart supervisor (dashboard Restart becomes a shutdown) and no PYTHONUTF8 environment (only -X utf8).
gaps.fix_hint: Point the Run key at Start-Apex-Platform.cmd (or run_apex_qwen.py --fast --resident).
gaps.how_confirmed: Read the code; not exercised on Windows.

gaps.issue: agent/threads.py (the memory 'serendipity engine') is dead code: its table is created, but nothing surfaces it.
gaps.fix_hint: Wire it to a dashboard card or delete it.
gaps.how_confirmed: grep for imports of agent.threads outside tests found none.

gaps.issue: Smart routing cannot be turned on from .env, and even if enabled it does nothing for DeepSeek (the cheap model is Claude and routing never crosses provider).
gaps.fix_hint: Make it env-readable and default ROUTING_SIMPLE_MODEL to the active provider's cheap model.

needs_from_owner: Re-run Start-Apex-Platform.cmd after pulling the UTF-8 fix and paste ~/.apex/resident.log if it stops again (the charmap crash fix has not been tried on the laptop).
Check the tray icon appears and Ctrl+Space starts a turn; tell us if Ctrl+Space clashes with a Windows keyboard-language shortcut on your PC.
Check that DEEPSEEK_API_KEY is in C:\Users\alexk\Apex\.env and AGENT_MODEL=deepseek-flash.
Open the dashboard budget panel (/api/budget) and check daily_reserved after a power cut; if it is not 0 while nothing is running, stuck reservations are eating your cap.
Decide whether you want resident mode to be able to run Python/skills/images at all; today it always refuses them.
Say whether you used the morning briefing or scheduled reminders; both are affected by the UTC/timezone bugs.
If you want Apex to start at login, say so: the current autostart skips your platform launcher.

rating.why: The core loop, budget and safety are well built and heavily tested, but in your real resident mode with DeepSeek, sub-agents are off, risky tools are always refused, the briefing scheduler is broken, schedules are in UTC, and network errors skip the fallback and can hang.
